clauses.reason: Terminated on 2018-04-20 by Executive Order 13830 (83 FR 18191), section 8(c): it supersedes Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended, and section 4 of EO 13830 prescribes the award of the Legion of Merit, which covers this clause, so the supersession extinguished the clause; no deferred effective date is stated, so it took effect when signed on April 20, 2018 (alternative: Federal Register publication, April 25, 2018, is not an effective date in the text). This clause is paragraph 1, which provides that the Legion of Merit shall be awarded by the President or at his direction to members of the armed forces of the United States and of the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines, and of friendly foreign nations, who after the proclamation of an emergency on September 8, 1939 distinguish themselves by exceptionally meritorious conduct in outstanding services. Later event: EO 10600 (March 15, 1955) restated this paragraph. Before: awards to members of the armed forces of the United States and of the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines, and of friendly foreign nations. After: awards to members of the armed forces of the United States and of friendly foreign nations (the Philippine Commonwealth members are no longer separately named); the rest of the paragraph is unchanged. The clause continues, amended. Actor of the end: EO 13830.

Terminated on 2018-04-20 by Executive Order 13830 (83 FR 18191), section 8(c): it supersedes Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended, and section 4 of EO 13830 prescribes the award of the Legion of Merit, which covers this clause, so the supersession extinguished the clause; no deferred effective date is stated, so it took effect when signed on April 20, 2018 (alternative: Federal Register publication, April 25, 2018, is not an effective date in the text). This clause is paragraph 2, which provides that awards may be proposed to the President by the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy, each acting on the recommendation of an officer with personal knowledge of the services. Later event: EO 10600 (March 15, 1955) restated this paragraph. Before: proposals by the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy. After: proposals by the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy and the Secretary of the Air Force, on the same recommendation basis. The clause continues, amended. Actor of the end: EO 13830.

Terminated on 2018-04-20 by Executive Order 13830 (83 FR 18191), section 8(c): it supersedes Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended, and section 4 of EO 13830 prescribes the award of the Legion of Merit, which covers this clause, so the supersession extinguished the clause; no deferred effective date is stated, so it took effect when signed on April 20, 2018 (alternative: Federal Register publication, April 25, 2018, is not an effective date in the text). This clause is paragraph 3, which provides that recommendations for awards to members of the armed forces of friendly foreign nations shall be submitted to the President for approval. Later event: EO 10600 (March 15, 1955) restated this paragraph. Before: all recommendations for awards to foreign members go to the President for approval. After: paragraph 3(a) lets the Secretary of Defense or his designee award the degrees of Commander, Officer and Legionnaire to foreign members after concurrence by the Secretary of State, and paragraph 3(b) requires the Secretary of Defense, after concurrence by the Secretary of State, to submit recommendations for the degree of Chief Commander to the President. The substance of the clause changed; it continues, amended. Actor of the end: EO 13830.

research_rationale:
EO 9260 (October 29, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt), titled Legion of Merit, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9260.txt; 7 FR 8819, PDF pages 1-1; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF). Identity: the extracted page carries the heading Executive Order 9260 and the title Legion of Merit; the order prescribes rules for the decoration created by the act of July 20, 1942 (Public Law 671, 77th Congress), under section 2 of that act. Inventory: the preamble (authority) commands nothing; the three numbered paragraphs are the operative clauses and the inventory is complete. Amendment: Executive Order 10600 (Dwight D. Eisenhower, March 15, 1955) amends paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 by restating each of them. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling each clause continues, amended, and the amendment is recorded as a later event with the before-and-after text in the clause reason; the amendment of paragraph 3 changes its substance. First end: Executive Order 13830 (April 20, 2018, 83 FR 18191) section 8(c) states that it supersedes Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended; EO 13830 section 4 prescribes who may award the Legion of Merit, in which degrees, and how recommendations for the highest degree reach the President, which covers the subject of all three clauses. It states no deferred effective date, so it took effect when signed. All three clauses are recorded as ended on 2018-04-20 and the whole order ends on that date. EO 13830 section 8(c) keeps existing regulations prescribed pursuant to the superseded orders in effect so far as consistent until modified or revoked by the Secretaries; those are subordinate regulations, not clauses of EO 9260, and section 8(d) says the order does not invalidate awards made earlier.

savings.reason: Awards made before 2018-04-20 remain valid: EO 13830 section 8(d) states that it does not invalidate any award of military decorations made before its effective date. Existing regulations prescribed pursuant to EO 9260 and the other superseded order remain in effect, so far as consistent with EO 13830, until modified or revoked under section 8(c); they are regulations, not commands of EO 9260.
